subsystems.name: Observational input layer
subsystems.role: supplies measured stellar ages, metallicities, orbits and exoplanet occurrence rates.

subsystems.name: Galactic chemical evolution model
subsystems.role: tracks how heavy elements spread through the galaxy over billions of years.

subsystems.name: Hazard model
subsystems.role: estimates how often nearby supernovae and gamma-ray bursts would sterilise a planet.

subsystems.name: Galactic dynamics
subsystems.role: places stars and planetary systems in space and time as the galaxy evolves.

subsystems.name: Habitability criteria
subsystems.role: converts physical conditions into a probability that complex life could arise and persist.

subsystems.name: Statistical inference
subsystems.role: propagates uncertainties and compares competing scenarios.

buildSteps.title: Compile a stellar catalogue
buildSteps.detail: Gather ages, metallicities and orbits for large samples of stars from surveys such as Gaia and ground-based spectroscopic campaigns.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate chemical evolution
buildSteps.detail: Fit star formation history and metal yields so the model reproduces observed abundance gradients across the galaxy.

buildSteps.title: Map explosion rates
buildSteps.detail: Use observed distributions of supernova progenitors and the cosmic star formation history to predict how often explosions occur in each region.

buildSteps.title: Convert explosions to radiation dose
buildSteps.detail: Model how shock fronts and gamma-ray jets deposit energy into nearby planetary atmospheres and surfaces.

buildSteps.title: Set habitability thresholds
buildSteps.detail: Define the minimum metallicity needed for rocky planets, the maximum radiation dose a biosphere can survive, and the time required for complex life to evolve.

buildSteps.title: Combine into spatio-temporal contours
buildSteps.detail: Overlay chemical, hazard and dynamical maps at different epochs to produce habitability contours that move as the galaxy changes.

buildSteps.title: Run sensitivity analysis
buildSteps.detail: Vary uncertain assumptions — such as GRB beaming angles or the metallicity threshold — to see which galaxies remain plausible hosts.

buildSteps.title: Compare with observed galaxies
buildSteps.detail: Check whether the model predicts the right number and distribution of habitable planets in galaxies of different masses and types.

buildSteps.title: Publish a predictive framework
buildSteps.detail: Turn the model into testable forecasts for future telescopes searching for biosignatures in specific galactic environments.

prerequisites.why: occurrence rates of rocky planets from Kepler and TESS are needed to connect habitable zones to actual worlds.
Gaia and spectroscopic surveys provide the ages, chemistry and motions that anchor the model.
local rates are observed, but extrapolating them across cosmic time and galaxy types remains uncertain.
lab and atmospheric studies exist, but tolerance limits for unknown biospheres are poorly constrained.
modelling a galaxy’s chemical and dynamical evolution requires substantial computing power.

pathway.milestone: models using simple metallicity gradients and supernova rates produce broad habitable annuli
pathway.unlocks: a first-order picture of which parts of a galaxy could host complex life.

pathway.milestone: incorporate Gaia-era ages and migration plus TESS and JWST exoplanet statistics
pathway.unlocks: contours that evolve with the galaxy rather than being static.

pathway.milestone: apply the framework to individual galaxies, including dwarfs and the Milky Way’s neighbours
pathway.unlocks: comparisons between galactic environments and their likely biosignature yield.

pathway.milestone: test predictions with next-generation telescopes targeting the most promising systems
pathway.unlocks: observational checks on whether galactic habitable zones are real or merely theoretical.
